dimensions.evidence: USD input annual times dimensionless UPV factor yields USD output; rate and years dimensionless. Variables table consistent (annual_saving/USD, discount_rate/1, period_count/1, present_value/USD). Matches UMD dimensional statement.

guards-inverses.evidence: 7 rejection cases verified present and correctly reasoned: rate 1.5 and 1.0 exceed the 10% ceiling; rate 0 (zero divisor, separate PV=annual*years branch); rate -0.05; years 0 and 101; missing years. Inverse notes hold: annual linear; rate has no exact form and the finite bracket (0,0.1] admits bisection (independently reproduced root 0.0300034523647); years enumerates guarded integers 1..100; years=1 substitution annual/(1+rate) exact at 50 digits. Zero-rate branch kept separate, never a guard relaxation.

reference-independence.evidence: Three published oracles reproduced via the closed form within stated rounding tolerances: NIST Table 5-2 $7,000/20yr/3% -> $104,139 (closed form 104,142.324, tol 5); UMD A=100/i=10%/n=8 -> 533.49 (closed form 533.49262, tol 0.01); NIST Table 5-3 $8,000/20yr -> $119,016 (forward at 3% 119,019.799, tol 5). Fourth reference is a curator boundary check explicitly labeled not a published case. Implied-rate inversion independently recomputed at 50 digits: Newton root 0.03000345236486 matches quoted 0.030003452365 (12dp); its residual -1.50e-07 matches stated 1.5e-07; bisection value 0.0300034523 residual 7.14e-05 matches stated 7.0e-05; r1 8dp quote 0.03000345 residual 2.60e-03 matches the corrected note. Independent bisection converges to the same root.

rights-provenance.evidence: NIST HB 135-2020 is a US federal publication available free of charge; DOI 10.6028/NIST.HB.135-2020 verified in-document (PDF p.1); record stores no verbatim excerpts, only paraphrase plus published factor values as recomputed oracles. UMD tutorial footer states Copyright (c) 1996-1998 Dept of Civil Engineering with no open-license statement; record states exactly this. Wikipedia text freely licensed, paraphrase only. Version/terms locations inspected and accurately qualified. This check records provenance only and does not grant legal clearance.

scope.evidence: Bounded scope explicit: home-A valuation-date in constant real prices, annual-effective real rate in (0,0.1], integer years 1..100, year-end constant amounts. rate<=0.1 ceiling is published-scope: NIST HB 135 s.3.3.2 (PDF p.67/printed p.35) quotes 10 CFR 436 bounding the real DOE discount rate between 3% and 10%, and Ch.5 cases price at the 3% floor. Boundary reference moved to rate=0.1 and rate=1.0/1.5 rejections cite the ceiling. Above-ceiling regimes and the zero-rate limit branch are deferred to separate records. Supersession resolved: duplicate_of uniform-present-value@source-3 declared with instruction to retire source-3 on admission so no duplicate coexists; this single-record batch stages nothing in the registry.

source-fidelity.evidence: Expression annual*((1+rate)^years-1)/(rate*(1+rate)^years) transcribes the UMD boxed Equal-Payment-Series Present-Worth Factor P=A*([1+i]^n-1)/(i*[1+i]^n) verbatim with exact symbol map (A->annual, i->rate, n->years, P->pv). NIST Eq.3-7 on PDF p.61 (printed p.29) gives PV=A0*((1+d)^t-1)/(d*(1+d)^t), the same form. Wikipedia annuity-immediate factor (1-(1+i)^-n)/i is algebraically identical. All NIST locators verified by extraction: PDF p.61 s.3.2.2.1/Eq.3-7/$457.97 example (recomputed 457.9707); PDF p.67 s.3.3.2 3%-10% bounds; PDF pp.98-106 Table 5-1/s.5.1.2/Tables 5-2..5-5 with UPV20=14.877, $104,139 and $119,016 rows; PDF p.160 s.8.6.6.1 with 2.15% non-DOE rate. #page=61 fragment lands on the UPV definition page, so it is the best single locator and the r1 stale-fragment claim is properly retracted. Evidence wording is qualified throughout (paraphrases, rounding allowances, no empirical claims).

models.permitted_use: Compute present value of a uniform year-end series in constant real prices for the home-A valuation-date context only, with annual-effective real rate in (0,0.1] and integer years 1..100. Not for above-10% regimes, zero or negative rates, escalated or maintenance-difference cashflows, or empirical savings claims.
